newsitem.title: UK: Med Suezmax tankers perk up, VLCCs quiet.
newsitem.headline: Med Suezmax tankers perk up, VLCCs quiet.

text.p: The Mediterranean 130,000 tonne dirty tanker market perked up on Wednesday with a spate of fixtures after several few weeks in the doldrums, brokers said.

"Med Suezmaxes (130,000 tonners) have been very quiet but they are starting to get busy after there were reports of six or seven done yesterday. It looks like rates are going to increase," one broker said.
Brokers put Med Suezmax rates at W90-95, depending on the age of the ship, some five to 10 points up from the last couple of weeks, while West Africa/U.S. Gulf Suezmaxes were steady at W95.

Meanwhile, Med Aframaxes (80,000 tonners) were little changed at W115-125, with prompt dates and Black Sea fixtures at the higher end of the range. Inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 tonne cargoes were also flat at W100.
The very large crude carrier (VLCC) market was quiet in both the Middle East and West Africa, brokers said.

Two Mideast VLCCs were fixed at a low W50 -- the 250,000 tonne Knock More on a trip Mideast/Singapore for Chevron, loading May 1, and the 244,000 tonne Leonidas Mideast/Thailand for Thai Petrochemical, loading April 27. But both are elderly ships built in 1974 and the Leonidas suffered engine trouble earlier this year on a trip from Iraq to South Africa, spending 63 days at sea on what is normally a two-week voyage.
Brokers said W52.5/55 was a more typical rate for a good quality ship Mideast/Singapore, and W62.5 Mideast/Japan, while West Africa/USG VLCCs remained at W72.5.

On fuel oil, inter-U.K./Cont 25,000 tonne cargoes dipped to W187.5 from W190 on plentiful prompt tonnage, while in the cross-Med market they firmed to W215 from W205 on a lack of vessels, brokers said.
The Caribs/upcoast market was uneventful, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes steady at W220/230 and 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil little changed at W205/220.
